claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: The structural solution is safety-gated deployment with objective pre-deployment standards — analogous to institutional review boards — that can be met in weeks or months, not years.
claims.speaker: safetyist
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: Administrators who authorize deployment without meeting governance thresholds must face institutional accountability, because without personal consequences the incentive to skip safety steps will always win.
claims.speaker: safetyist
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: A 90-day expiration converts a safety gate into a deployment countdown and incentivizes vendors to overwhelm review capacity and run out the clock
claims.speaker: safetyist
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: Pre-deployment verification is the established norm in pharmaceuticals, aviation, nuclear energy, and medical devices — what is genuinely untested is concurrent governance in education
claims.speaker: safetyist
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: AI is already reshaping university admissions scoring, financial aid modeling, academic advising, and faculty performance evaluation with no faculty governance, no student visibility, and no consent mechanism
claims.speaker: safetyist
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: Administrative AI in education is that terrain — the classroom debate is secondary.
claims.speaker: skeptic
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: The contractual audit guarantee is the weakest link in the Safetyist's architecture.
claims.speaker: skeptic
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: AI is already making high-stakes decisions about who gets admitted to university, who receives financial aid, and which students get flagged for academic advising interventions — no pre-deployment gate governs these systems
claims.speaker: accelerationist
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: The FDA did not solve pharmaceutical safety by banning drug development until governance caught up — it created an external mandate requiring funded safety infrastructure as a condition of bringing products to market
claims.speaker: accelerationist
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: Delay does not protect under-resourced students from AI — it protects them from governed AI while leaving them exposed to ungoverned AI
claims.speaker: accelerationist
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: Educational AI harms are diffuse, gradual, and largely reversible — the appropriate comparison is textbook selection or pedagogical method adoption, not FDA drug approval
claims.speaker: accelerationist
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: When an algorithm miscalculates a student's financial aid eligibility, that student may lose a semester or drop out entirely — these harms are functionally irreversible for the individuals affected.
claims.speaker: safetyist
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: Conditioning federal Title IV financial aid eligibility on institutional compliance with a mandatory AI system inventory and tiered review framework is the specific external mandate mechanism.
claims.speaker: safetyist
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: Vendors who refuse audit bear strict liability — financially responsible for every harm their opaque system causes, with no safe-harbor defense — making audit refusal economically irrational.
claims.speaker: safetyist
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: Governed institutional deployment is the equity intervention, but governed means governed: institutions deploying AI without tiered review are not solving the equity problem, they are importing it.
claims.speaker: safetyist
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: The Gainful Employment Rule was proposed under Obama in 2014, gutted under Trump in 2019, and only partially restored under Biden — that is the recent track record of the exact enforcement vehicle being proposed
claims.speaker: skeptic
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: Strict liability on paper becomes negotiated liability in practice when the vendor has more lawyers than the university system has compliance staff
claims.speaker: skeptic
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: The democratic floor is not a seat at the table but the right to know when a machine has made a decision about you, and the right to say no
claims.speaker: skeptic
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: A student wrongly denied admission or stripped of financial aid by a miscalibrated algorithm suffers a harm that no later correction can fully undo.
claims.speaker: accelerationist
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: Already-deployed administrative systems get a mandatory provisional audit within 45 days — if that audit reveals error rates or disparate impact above a defined threshold, the system is suspended pending remediation.
claims.speaker: accelerationist
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: Any AI system that makes or materially influences a decision about a specific student must notify that student that AI was involved, identify the specific system and its vendor, and provide a human review pathway with a defined 15-business-day response window.
claims.speaker: accelerationist
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: An open-ended review with no countdown clock lets ungoverned systems keep making life-altering decisions while regulators deliberate.
claims.speaker: safetyist
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: Strict gates applied only to new systems reward vendors who deployed fastest during the ungoverned period, creating a regulatory moat that protects incumbents not because their systems are safer but because they moved first.
claims.speaker: safetyist
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: Statutory non-waivable minimum liability provisions, institutional consortia, and mandatory public disclosure of audit results prevent liability from being quietly negotiated away.
claims.speaker: safetyist
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: The 45-day audit assumes a solved problem — vendor cooperation — that is actually the unsolved problem.
claims.speaker: skeptic
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: Notification without the right to refuse is a formality — it tells the student an algorithm decided their financial aid package and records their powerlessness.
claims.speaker: skeptic
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: Open-weight models satisfy the audit-access requirement by construction — their transparency is the audit.
claims.speaker: accelerationist
claims.debate_title: USC use of AI

claims.claim_text: At least one enforcement layer must be genuinely decentralized: mandatory public release of anonymized audit data and fairness metrics.
claims.speaker: accelerationist
